title: Negative Results Stay Unpublished
bottleneck: Null and negative findings are systematically harder to publish, creating a file-drawer problem that biases meta-analyses and sends multiple labs down the same dead ends. Journals favor striking positives, and researchers rationally withhold failed experiments. Meta-analyses that ignore the file drawer systematically overestimate effect sizes, misleading policy and follow-up research.
why_it_blocks: Science cannot efficiently map what does not work, so effort is duplicated and effect sizes are inflated across fields. The published record becomes a highlight reel rather than an honest map of inquiry.
current_state: Preprint servers and null-results journals absorb some of the flow, but prestige publishing still selects for positivity. Mandatory pre-registration of all studies, not just trials, would help but faces steep adoption barriers. Funders could fix much of this by requiring registration as a grant condition.
